info.name: Cerberus
info.description:
Full REST + GraphQL surface for the Cerberus auth service.

**Setup**
1. Import `Cerberus.dev.postman_environment.json`.
2. Set `baseUrl` to your running server (default `http://localhost:3000`).
3. Run `OAuth2 > POST /v1/oauth/token — password grant` — the test script auto-saves the bearer token into the env.

**Conventions**
- Every authenticated REST endpoint expects `Authorization: Bearer {{bearerToken}}`.
- Phase-11 placeholder endpoints (change-password, MFA, audit-log/me, update-display-name) expect `Authorization: {{userId}}` instead.
- TOTP codes are auto-computed by the prerequest script of `/mfa/confirm`, `/mfa/disable`, `/mfa/verify`, and the GraphQL MFA mutations.
- GraphQL endpoints all hit `POST /graphql`; the request body is a `{query, variables}` envelope.
- Error responses include `code` (REST) or `extensions.code` (GraphQL) with stable strings — switch on those in client code.

request.description: Unauthenticated liveness probe. Used by load balancers and Kubernetes liveness.
Unauthenticated readiness probe. Checks Postgres + Redis. Returns 200 only when both are reachable.
Authenticate with email + password. Returns a sessionId and familyId for the new session.
Rotate the refresh token. Returns a new pair. The old refresh token is consumed.
Revoke the session identified by the presented refresh token. Idempotent.
List all active sessions for the authenticated user. V1 uses the Phase-11 Authorization placeholder header (Phase 13 JWT auth replaces this). Both headers are sent for clarity.

request.description: Revoke a specific session. Must be your own session (cross-user revoke returns 404). V1 uses Authorization.
Issue an access token (JWT) via the Resource Owner Password Credentials grant. The response is the OAuth2 standard shape.
Exchange a refresh token for a new access token (RFC 6749 §6).
RFC 7662 token introspection. Returns {active: true, ...} when valid; {active: false} otherwise.
RFC 7009 token revocation. Always returns 200 OK (per spec).
JWKS document with all currently-verifying public keys. Resource servers fetch this on startup.
Operator-only. Mint a new RSA signing key. The previous key is retired with a grace window.
Register a new user. Open to unauthenticated callers. Auto-creates a personal organization when no slug is supplied AND no email-domain matches.
Change the authenticated user's password. Emits identity.password.changed — all sessions are revoked.
Update the authenticated user's display name.
Remove the display name.
Begin MFA enrollment. Returns the TOTP secret and 10 recovery codes (returned ONCE).
Confirm MFA enrollment with a 6-digit TOTP code. The prerequest script computes the TOTP from {{mfaSecret}}.
